page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.4xlarge is an ARMv9-based general-purpose instance powered by AWS Neoverse-V2 cores managed by the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with one thread per core, accompanied by a 36 MB L3 cache. It supplies 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Storage is provisioned via an integrated 950 GB local NVMe SSD, and baseline network throughput is rated at 8 Gbps. The instance does not include discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a high-throughput memory subsystem, with PassMark memory testing reaching top-tier percentiles and large-block uncached read and write bandwidth ranking in the top quartile. Compute operations reflect strong multi-core scalability, achieving upper-quartile scores in multi-threaded Geekbench execution and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In contrast, single-core benchmarks, Clang compilation, and ray tracing align with median results. Database operations perform within the top 25%, while Redis key-value operations and static web serving register at industry-standard medians. Large-scale transformer prompt processing exhibits lower throughput, reflecting CPU-only execution characteristics.

By incorporating 950 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage alongside dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores, the instance provides cost-efficient I/O density by removing the need for external network storage on scratch volumes. The configuration is optimal for distributed database nodes, caching layers, continuous integration build jobs, and containerized backend web services requiring consistent core allocation and high local disk throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.4xlarge is an ARMv9 general-purpose cloud instance powered by 16 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz under the Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 64 GB of RAM, adhering to a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, alongside an integrated 950 GB local NVMe SSD and 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With no integrated GPUs, performance focuses heavily on memory throughput and multi-threaded CPU tasks. Benchmark profiles demonstrate top-tier memory subsystem results alongside top-quartile performance in multi-core metrics, decompression tasks, and database operations. Single-thread processing and Redis throughput remain within average parameters. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage delivers qualitative cost efficiency by mitigating external disk dependencies for I/O-intensive workloads. The instance is structured for transactional databases, CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration, and general-purpose backend services.
